amina: opened PR to document websocket/streaming metering and add a TS SDK example. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/6218
amina: TL;DR: add header guidance for streaming clients, show per-chunk vs per-finalize billing, and update dashboards + alert thresholds for stream-heavy tenants.
jon: looks important. quick Q: are we adding a new header or reusing X-Redwood-Usage?
lev: prefer reuse so backend reuses same ingest path. proposed header form for streaming: `X-Redwood-Usage: acct=acct_99;units=1;unit_type=tokens;stream=true`
jon: ok. I'll author a TypeScript SDKv2 snippet showing websocket client that sets the header and emits per-chunk usage. will redact keys.
jon: snippet I plan to add:
```ts
import { StreamingClient } from '@redwood/inference-sdk';
const client = new StreamingClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
const ws = await client.openStream({
  url: 'wss://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream',
  headers: { 'X-Redwood-Usage': 'acct=acct_99;units=1;unit_type=tokens;stream=true' }
});
ws.sendChunk({ text: 'hello' }); // billed per-chunk according to header units
ws.finalize(); // finalization may bill additional tokens
```
lev: add a short note: when `stream=true` the runtime accumulates chunk units and emits rollups into minute buckets; finalization can trigger additional unit accounting for post-processing.
tara: please also add an example calc for embeddings vs generation in the same PR. embeddings should show per-vector tokenization + encoding overhead (e.g., 1 request -> 256 vector_tokens) so customers see why embeddings bills differently.
amina: good call. also update the pricing table row for the "professional" tier we've renamed to "scale". include a migration note for customers who used the old label.
jon: ops question: should docs recommend a dashboard alert threshold for stream-heavy tenants? e.g., 1k tokens/min average?
ops-bot: recommend baseline alerts: rate > 500 tokens/min (warning) and >2000 tokens/min (critical) per-tenant for burst-sensitive workloads. note: panel ids differ between staging/prod — link to dashboard slug `/d/usage/streaming-overview` and use `?var-customer=$customer` for durable pre-selection. OPS-1178 opened to evaluate redirects for legacy anchors.
lev: I'll add PromQL examples for both minute view and invoice window:
- minute: `sum(rate(redwood_stream_tokens_total[1m])) by (customer)`
- monthly: `sum(increase(redwood_stream_tokens_total[30d])) by (customer)`
jon: adding those to the PR. also because streaming clients often misinterpret burst credits, we'll add a tiny ASCII timeline showing: chunk billing -> minute rollup -> burst credit applied -> overflow -> fallback routing (if configured).
tara: editorial note: in the quota doc change wording from "requests are blocked" to "requests may be routed to fallback model or receive 429 depending on customer's routing policy". saves us from support confusion.
amina: good. Also add a short FAQ entry: "Do cached stream chunks count?" Answer: cached responses that avoid model forward-pass do not increment billed tokens; only cache misses and finalization frames count.
docs-bot: Preview deployed: https://deploy-preview-6218--docs.redwood.ai — check the TS snippet renders and the timeline SVG on staging.
amina: I'll do a quick pass and merge if staging looks green. target: ship before docs freeze tomorrow. ping me on slack if anything 404s. :thumbsup:
